title: Charcoal Briquettes 8kg

drivers.name: Holiday: Independence Day
drivers.evidence: Historical median x1.57 vs baseline (2024, 2025); noise-adjusted x1.0. But 2024-07-01: x1.63, 2025-06-30: x1.51. Recent 30% off week (2026-04-06) sold x2.53, but no holiday. This event is stronger than past 25% off events.

drivers.name: Promotion: 25% off
drivers.evidence: Past 25% off: 2024-05-13 (x1.59), 2025-10-06 (x0.78). Median x0.83, noise-adjusted x1.0. 2026-04-06 (30% off) had x2.53. This is a deeper discount than prior 25% off events. But 2026-06-01 (15% off) gave x0.83. So effect is uncertain. Shrink toward 1.0.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 45.6. Independence Day shows a strong historical lift (x1.57 vs baseline, noise-adjusted x1.0), but recent weeks show no such spike. The 25% discount is deeper than past 25% off events (2024-05-13: x1.59, 2025-10-06: x0.78), but the 30% off in 2026-04-06 gave x2.53. However, that week had no holiday. The classical uplift model underestimates due to noise adjustment. A 25% off on a holiday should lift demand, but the prior 15% off had no lift (x0.83). The 2026-04-06 30% off was an outlier. We adjust up for the holiday and promotion, but shrink toward 1.0 due to thin evidence and noise. No pantry-loading effect expected as this is not a repeat promotion week. The 5%-95% range remains calibrated.

  shelf price: 11.97 (-25.0% vs regular price 15.96)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 45.6 | 5%-95%: 29.2 - 79.6 | 10%-90%: 31.7 - 64.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-67% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
